instructionalProposals.teachingUnderstanding: Recognize Authentication Header as IPsec integrity/data-origin authentication without encryption; network-protocol context, precise numbered scope withheld.
instructionalProposals.contentQualification: Retain no-encryption boundary. AH protection excludes mutable header fields; replay resistance needs receiver checks and sound security-association/key handling. Source authentication is not unique-person attribution or evidence of safe plaintext. Inherited 1.4/3.1 tags and acronym-list presence do not establish an assessed IPsec configuration skill.

instructionalProposals.teachingUnderstanding: Recognize ephemeral finite-field Diffie-Hellman key agreement as supporting session forward secrecy under protocol and secret-handling prerequisites.
instructionalProposals.contentQualification: HOLD automatic perfect protection: appropriate groups, fresh ephemeral private values, authenticated exchange and secure erasure matter. Agreement does not itself encrypt application data, sign it or authenticate the peer. The card does not prove a deployed session property or endpoint protection; preserve separate DH and DHE support identities.

instructionalProposals.teachingUnderstanding: Recognize ephemeral elliptic-curve Diffie-Hellman key agreement; this is distinct from ECDSA signature generation.
instructionalProposals.contentQualification: HOLD forward-secrecy guarantee from the name alone: suitable curves/parameters, fresh ephemeral secrets, authenticated protocol binding, correct implementation and disposal remain required. ECDHE is not ECDSA, generic ECC, bulk encryption or automatic post-quantum safety. No exchange, parameter validation or session-key derivation was executed.

instructionalProposals.teachingUnderstanding: Recognize ECDSA as a signature-generation/verification algorithm; not encryption or key exchange.
instructionalProposals.contentQualification: Retain signature role only: sign with the designated private signature key and verify with the corresponding trusted public key/parameters. Neither confidentiality, key agreement nor truthfulness follows from a valid signature. Secure per-signature value generation and key custody matter; approved deterministic signing is not blanket nonce reuse. No signature operation or non-repudiation deployment was verified.

instructionalProposals.teachingUnderstanding: Recognize PEM-style text encoding for cryptographic objects such as certificates and keys; certificate-format context with precise numbered scope withheld.
instructionalProposals.contentQualification: HOLD any inference that text/Base64 or a PEM label encrypts a private key, establishes issuer/hostname/path trust, or proves valid syntax. The encoded object may be a certificate, public key, unencrypted or encrypted private-key structure; inspect its type/protection separately. PEM is not PKCS, DER or certificate validation, and the exact glossary is narrower than the card.

instructionalProposals.teachingUnderstanding: Recognize forward secrecy as a property of established sessions limiting the effect of later long-term authentication-key compromise.
instructionalProposals.contentQualification: HOLD absolute protects past sessions wording: later long-term authentication-key theft should not recover earlier session secrets when the design and erasure premises hold. PFS is not a cipher, certificate type, key length or mere fresh-session-key label; it does not protect already stolen session keys, compromised endpoint plaintext or future sessions after key theft.

instructionalProposals.teachingUnderstanding: Recognize PKCS as a standards family, not one algorithm, certificate format or universal operation; precise numbered scope withheld.
instructionalProposals.contentQualification: HOLD bare-family ambiguity: specify numbered standard/version/task before inferring behavior. PKCS #1 RSA schemes, #8 private-key syntax, #10 certification requests and #12 identity exchange are different purposes. No universal encryption, key inclusion, trust, compatibility or safe-export guarantee follows from PKCS naming; no format/API/parser or migration was tested.

instructionalProposals.teachingUnderstanding: Recognize a pre-established shared secret used by an authentication protocol; authentication/key-custody context with precise numbered scope withheld.
instructionalProposals.contentQualification: HOLD manual/static-only and automatic secure-authentication interpretations: PSKs can be externally provisioned or derived from an earlier session, and possession authenticates only under the chosen protocol and custody/identity policy. Use adequate secret entropy, protection and replacement after compromise; multiple holders defeat unique-holder attribution. A PSK alone does not imply forward secrecy; password-strength assumptions and selected key-exchange mode matter.
